short_summary: A travel writer explores the traditional pre-dinner drink and snack culture across various local bars in Verona, Italy.

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.title: My search for the perfect Italian aperitivo in Verona

paragraphs: In Italy, the aperitivo is a well-known ritual of having a drink and a small bite to eat before a meal. However, this custom changes depending on the city. While Milan and Venice have their own styles, Verona follows a unique tradition centered around the osteria, a traditional local tavern where people often enjoy a glass of wine and a small snack while standing at the counter.

A writer recently explored this drinking culture in Verona to see how the local custom works. Interestingly, the writer noticed that the ritual does not strictly wait for the evening. One morning at about 9:30 am, people were already ordering small glasses of white wine, sparkling wine, and spritzes without anyone finding it unusual.

The search led to several different spots across the city. At Monte Baldo, an establishment operating since 1909, the writer enjoyed a traditional-method sparkling wine from Piedmont alongside small open sandwiches known as tartine, topped with creamy stockfish spread and boiled egg with anchovy. Another traditional wine spot offered fine sparkling wine with cured pork and gorgonzola cream, where staff explained the wine choices to a queue of visitors.

Further exploring the city, the writer visited Tor-Tor, located behind the Arena, which featured a strong selection of natural wines and small savoury meatballs recommended by experts. Across the Adige river in Veronetta, a neighbourhood local named Ai Preti offered a relaxed atmosphere with local crowds, affordable wine, and snacks priced under ten euros in total. Another stop, Velvet, occupied part of a historic fifteenth-century building and provided a handsome counter and drinks that came with extra snacks like cashews and small pastries.

Finally, the writer visited Morandin twice, noting that it had a very local crowd, a large selection of traditional cicchetti small plates, and crisp local sparkling wine. Although the writer originally intended just to have a quick drink before dinner, the experience at Morandin made staying for the evening meal irresistible.

facts.fact: A writer explored the aperitivo culture in Verona, Italy, visiting various traditional osterias and bars.
In Verona, aperitivo can be enjoyed at any time of day, even starting as early as the morning hours.
The writer visited several specific venues including Monte Baldo, Tor-Tor, Ai Preti, Velvet, and Morandin, trying local wines and small snacks like tartine and polpette.
